sam: Quick sync — we need to lock down the client-facing error taxonomy before the canary on Fri. Seeing inconsistent messages between routing decisions and console badges.

kai: can you point to a concrete example?

sam: yes — when requests route to degraded-capacity tier we currently return 200 + body with \"warning\" field. Console shows a yellow badge but SDK surfaces 200 so product teams assume success.

priya: oof. That breaks observability for customers (and our SLAs). We should avoid returning 200 for anything that meaningfully degrades capacity or changes semantics.

linh: agreed. proposal: canonical error categories -> [\"client_error\",\"transient\",\"quota\",\"degraded_route\",\"internal\"]. Map to HTTP scope: client_error=4xx, transient/ quota=429/503 depending, degraded_route=409? or 503 semantics?

kai: prefer 409 for semantic conflict, but 503 makes it obvious it's degraded availability. telemetry/console will treat 503 as bad. Might be noisy.

michael: think about routing policy interactions: if fallback succeeded (slower model) we want to surface success but also badge the route as \"degraded\" and emit telemetry signal so customers can alert. We must not break existing integrations.

sam: right — three outcomes:
1) hard failure (no fallback) -> non-2xx, explicit error_type
2) soft fallback -> return 200 + body but with header x-redwood-degrade: soft and telemetry flag signal.routing.degraded=1
3) degraded but semantic change (model produces truncated tokens) -> non-2xx to force customer handling

linh: mixing 2) with a header + badge seems reasonable. But product asked for a single canonical client-visible field we can index in dashboards. I suggest `x-rw-status: degraded|ok|failed` header and `error_type` in response body when non-2xx.

priya: console UX needs mapping rules: badge colors, tooltip copy, and runbook links. Example mapping table in console: 503 -> \"Service degraded — may fall back to slower models\" tooltip -> link to docs/rollouts.

kai: also add quota edge: when a tenant hits soft quota and we route to reserve, send 429 with body {\"error_type\":\"quota_routed\",\"hint\":\"upgrade_or_backoff\"}. Do not return 200 in that case. Telemetry: signal.quota.routed=1 and sample keys.

michael: we should include examples for SDKs. e.g.
```json
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
x-rw-status: degraded
Content-Type: application/json
{
  \"error_type\": \"degraded_route\",
  \"message\": \"Routed to degraded pool (latency x2)\",
  \"retry_after\": 60
}
```

sam: love that. small checklist:
- [ ] header spec (x-rw-status) + allowed values
- [ ] canonical error_type set and mapping to http codes
- [ ] telemetry labels (signal.*) and sampling rules
- [ ] console badge mapping and tooltip text
- [ ] SDK docs + example responses + migration guide

linh: I'll draft the RFC for mapping and put in #eng-docs. Can we agree that fallback-success remains 200 but must include x-rw-status=degraded and signal?

priya: yes but only if semantics unchanged. If output quality or tokens are truncated -> non-2xx.

kai: +1. Also: add a small rollout gating step — the canary should opt-in header `x-rw-experiment-errors=v1` so existing clients don't break. Deploy-bot: schedule canary?

deploy-bot: canary started by @michael on canary/delivery at https://deploys/redwood/123 :rocket: (ts 1719997888)

michael: starting canary with opt-in header. I'll post results in this thread after 2h.

sam: thanks everyone — this clears the high-level. expect RFC from @linh today. :thumbsup:
